- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >5% gap), apply upward bias to align with recent trend; especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (≥0.40) and model is flat or declining, expect upward revision; increase forecast by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; if sentiment is negative and price is trending down, add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for lag.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating 0.18–0.44), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values to reduce erratic swings.
